title: The room prepared (Luke 22:1–13)
hookLine: Satan enters Judas; a man with a water jar leads to an upper room

lines: ONE OF THE TWELVE SLIPS AWAY.
FOLLOW A MAN WITH A WATER JAR.
cards: Two scenes, running at once in the same city.
In the first, the city is filling up for Passover, the feast of unleavened bread, and the chief priests and scribes are looking for a way to take Jesus quietly, because they fear the crowds.

One of the twelve slips away to meet them. In the second, two friends walk through crowded streets with strange directions: look for a man carrying a jar of water, and follow him home. One door opens to darkness.
The other opens to a guest.

teach.h: SATAN ENTERS ONE OF THE TWELVE.
teach.b: Luke says it in one line, in the King James words: "Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve." Not an outsider. One of the twelve Jesus had chosen by name.
Judas goes to the chief priests and the temple captains, and they're glad, and agree to give him money.
Luke doesn't explain why. People have guessed ever since: money, disappointment, politics. The text doesn't settle it, and it's honest to say so.
Now the other scene. Jesus sends Peter and John to get the Passover ready: "there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in."

teach.h: A MAN WITH A JAR STANDS OUT.
teach.b: Some readers suggest carrying water was more often women's work, so a man with a jar may have stood out, an easy sign to follow. They're to ask the owner where the guest room is.
"And he shall shew you a large upper room furnished: there make ready." The owner is never named. His room is simply furnished and ready for whoever the teacher sends.
Peter and John find everything as they were told, and make ready the Passover. Two doors. One opened for betrayal, quietly, for a price.
One opened for a meal, quietly, with no price named. The second, a stranger's spare room, is where Jesus will sit down to the Passover with his friends.

how: Christians remember the upper room on Maundy Thursday, the evening before Good Friday, and some congregations share a simple meal or set a table that night to recall it.

games.q: you're Peter, sent into a crowded festival city to find a room for the Passover. how do you find it?
o: ask at the temple for a free room.
follow a man carrying a jar of water.
wait at the gate for someone to offer.
games.why: "there shall a man meet you, bearing a pitcher of water; follow him into the house where he entereth in." the owner shows them a large upper room, furnished.

practice: Think of a space you have, even a small one, a spare chair, a corner of the kitchen table, and picture someone who could use a place to sit: a neighbor, a coworker eating alone.
Picture getting it ready for them, clearing the chair, putting out a glass of water, turning on the light, without inviting anyone yet. If you pray, ask God to send whoever needs it.

orig.note: Greek: a room upstairs, an upper room. the word Luke uses for the room where the Passover meal is held.
